info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package functions is your serverless code: publish it, call it over HTTP, watch every run and what it cost.

get.summary: Is every serverless function the caller's org has published, each with its real 7-day rollup.
get.description:
Is every serverless function the caller's org has published, each with its
real 7-day rollup.

A row carries the function's runtime, resource limits, deployment target and its
invoke endpoint, plus envCount — how many secrets it mounts. The rollup fields
are ABSENT rather than zero when the function has not run in the window, so a
console renders "—" instead of a fabricated 0.

Requires a validated principal; the listing is scoped to its org.

post.summary: Publishes a serverless function under the caller's org and answers 201 with it.
post.description:
Publishes a serverless function under the caller's org and answers 201
with it.

The name is the key and is claimed once; the names that would shadow a
collection route are reserved. runtime and environment are the same field —
either spelling is accepted — and default to node.

Bounds are clamped rather than refused where a clamp is honest: a timeout above
the 900-second ceiling becomes the ceiling instead of silently reverting to the
30-second default, and an omitted memory limit becomes 256Mi. target=fleet runs
on the org's own GPU fleet and supports runtime=python only.

Requires a validated principal; the function is owned by that principal's org.

get.summary: Is what is live right now — each function's current record IS its live deployment, so this is the deployment inventory.
get.description:
Is what is live right now — each function's current record IS its
live deployment, so this is the deployment inventory.

There is no deployment history behind it: a function has one record, and
publishing replaces it. The 7-day rollup is deliberately absent here, because
this read is about what is deployed rather than about how it has performed.

get.summary: Is the org's serverless dashboard over a window: a per-function invocation costLine and how those invocations ended.
get.description:
Is the org's serverless dashboard over a window: a per-function
invocation costLine and how those invocations ended.

Every point is a REAL count of rows that fell in that bucket — nothing is
interpolated or invented, so an empty window draws a flat line rather than a
fabricated one.

costCents is null and stays null: there is no per-invocation cost source to read,
and reporting a number computed some other way would be a guess presented as a
measurement. Requires a validated principal; the read is scoped to its org.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is 1H, 6H, 24H (the default), 7D or 30D. Anything else falls back to
24H rather than failing.

get.summary: Is the NAMES of the secrets the caller org's functions mount.
get.description:
Is the NAMES of the secrets the caller org's functions mount.

Values are NEVER read or returned — this surface knows which names a function
asks for and nothing about what is behind them, which is what makes it safe to
list at all. One row per distinct (namespace, name).

get.summary: Is what calls the caller org's functions — one row per function.
get.description:
Is what calls the caller org's functions — one row per function.

Every function has exactly one trigger today, its HTTP invoke endpoint, so this
is the function list read as "how is each of these reached".

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's functions and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's functions and answers 204.

A name this org does not hold is 404 — never a silent success — and a name
belonging to another tenant is the same 404, because the delete is predicated on
the validated org.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the function the URL names.

get.summary: Is one function with everything a detail page needs in one round-trip: its definition, its 7-day rollup, its trigger, its twenty most recent invocations and the NAMES of the secrets it mounts.
get.description:
Is one function with everything a detail page needs in one round-trip: its
definition, its 7-day rollup, its trigger, its twenty most recent invocations
and the NAMES of the secrets it mounts.

Secret values are never read or returned. A name the caller's org does not hold
is 404, which is also what another tenant's function looks like from here.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the function the URL names.

get.summary: Is one function's past runs, newest first — each with its status, HTTP code, method, time and duration.
get.description:
Is one function's past runs, newest first — each with its status,
HTTP code, method, time and duration.

These are real recorded rows, not a projection: an invocation appears here only
once it actually ran. Requires a validated principal; the read is scoped to its
org.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the function the URL names.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page, defaulting to 100.

post.summary: Runs a function and records a REAL invocation.
post.description:
Runs a function and records a REAL invocation.

The answer is the invocation record whatever happened to it: 200 when the org's
code ran clean, 502 when it ran and failed, 503 when this deployment has no
sandbox to run code in. The record IS the evidence, so it rides the failure
rather than being replaced by an error envelope.

Billing is two-part and both parts are prepaid-then-metered on the one shared
meter: a flat per-invocation request fee, gated BEFORE any sandbox compute runs
so an unfunded org gets 402 and nothing executes, and a usage-native
GB-seconds compute debit taken after the run. Either is independently free when
its fee is zero, so an operator can bill by request alone, by compute alone, or
by both — and a zero request fee removes the balance gate with it.

A TRANSPORT failure is not charged: the sandbox being unreachable ran no
billable compute. Code that ran and exited non-zero IS charged — that is a
successful invocation of a failing program, not a billing failure.

When the sandbox is not configured on this deployment, a non-fleet function
fails closed before anything is recorded — no execution and no fabricated
output. Scoped to the caller's org; requires a validated principal.

get.summary: Is the output of a function's most recent run — its error text when that run failed, else what it printed.
get.description:
Is the output of a function's most recent run — its error text when that
run failed, else what it printed.

It is the LAST run only, and it is empty when the function has never run. There
is no log retention behind this beyond the recorded invocation itself.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the function the URL names.

key.description: the function the line is about

points.description: one point per bucket, oldest first

code.description: Code is the source to run, capped so one function cannot amplify the store.

envNames.description:
EnvNames are the secret NAMES to mount. Values live in the secret store and
are never carried here.

environment.description:
Environment is a second spelling of runtime, accepted so a console that says
"environment" needs no translation.

handler.description: Handler is the entry point within the code.

image.description: Image names a prebuilt image to run instead of source.

memoryLimit.description:
MemoryLimit is the memory the function runs with, defaulting to 256Mi. It is
also the multiplier on the GB-seconds compute charge.

name.description:
Name is the function's org-unique handle and the segment that addresses it,
matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. The names that would shadow a
collection route are reserved.

namespace.description:
Namespace groups functions for display. It is cosmetic — the org is the
isolation key — and is normalised to a DNS-safe label.

runtime.description: Runtime is the language the code runs under: node, python or deno.

target.description:
Target is where the function runs: sandbox (the default) or fleet, the org's
own GPU fleet. fleet supports runtime=python only.

timeoutSec.description:
TimeoutSec is the per-invocation deadline, defaulting to 30 and clamped at
900 — a larger value is capped rather than reset to the default.

functions.description: Functions is one row per published function.

recentInvocations.description: RecentInvocations is its twenty most recent runs, newest first.

secrets.description: Secrets are the NAMES it mounts. Values are never read or returned.

triggers.description: Triggers is how this function is reached.

envCount.description: how many secret NAMES it mounts; values are never carried

errors7d.description: how many of those runs failed

image.description: the prebuilt image it runs, when it runs one instead of source

invocations7d.description: runs in the last 7 days; ABSENT, never 0, when it has not run

memoryLimit.description: the memory it runs with, and the multiplier on its compute charge

namespace.description: the display group it belongs to; the org is the isolation key

status.description: whether it is ready to serve

successRate.description: share of those runs that succeeded, 0..1

target.description: where it runs: empty for the sandbox, "fleet" for the org's GPU fleet

invocations.description: Invocations is one row per past run, newest first.

method.description: the HTTP method that triggered it

status.description: how the run ended: ok, error or timeout

statusCode.description:
Code is the status the function's OWN code answered with, which is not the
status of the reply — a program can answer 500 through a healthy sandbox.

input.description: Input is what the function is given on stdin. It is opaque to this surface.

logs.description:
Logs is that run's error text when it failed, else its output. It is empty
when the function has never run.

v.description: how many invocations fell in it — a real count, never interpolated

secrets.description:
Secrets is one row per distinct (namespace, name) a function mounts. Values
are NEVER read or returned.

mountedBy.description: MountedBy is a function that mounts it.

name.description: Name is the environment variable the function mounts.

namespace.description: Namespace is the group the mounting function belongs to.

success.description: invocations whose code ran and wrote nothing to stderr

timeout.description: invocations that hit their configured deadline

triggers.description: Triggers is one row per function, describing how it is reached.

type.description: what kind of trigger it is; HTTP is the only one today

series.description: one line per function that ran in the window

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
